findings.finding: Use f(n)=a−a/q where a=n−1, q=smallest divisor>2 of a. For M=3^{2025!}, a≡c (mod p) for p≤2025. Thus q=4 if a%4=0, else smallest odd prime dividing c (or 5081287 for c=10162574). Compute X=2025!. g(c)=⌊X(q−1)/q⌋/X. Sum p_i=∑⌊X(q_i−1)/q_i⌋, reduce p_total/X, output (p+q) mod 99991. (q’s:4,4,11,5081287,4,17). Result 40958. Pitfall: ensure a%4 check, handle large q not dividing X.

f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n. For n=M+ c (M=3^{2025!}), S≡c+1 (mod p≠3). So S’s primes = factors of c+1 (and 3^{v₃(c)}). Minimal lcm = D=S·k₁k₂/(k₁k₂+k₁+k₂) where (S·k₁)≡(S·k₂)≡0 (mod d). Search small (k₁,k₂). Results: g(0)=2/3; g(4M)=10/3 (pair 3,6); g(1848374)=16/25 (2,16); g(10162574)=30/47 (2,15); g(265710644)=64/97 (2,64); g(44636594)=110/167 (2,55). Sum = p/q → compute (p+q) mod 99991. Pitfall: ensure integer a,b via S·k_i≡0 (mod d).

Use f(S)=S−1−p_max where p_max is largest divisor of N=S−1 <N/2. For M=3^{2025!}, N0=M−1 has smallest odd divisor 5. For small c, d=smallest odd prime factor of c. For c=4M, smallest odd divisor of 5M−1 is 11549. Compute D=2025!. Then g(0)=1−1/5−1/D; g(c>0,d|D)=1−1/d; g(c,d∤D)=1−⌊D/d⌋/D−1/D; g(4M)=5−⌈5D/11549⌉/D. Sum → p/q, reduce, (p+q) mod 99991 = 13657. Pitfalls: handle c=0 negative ε, c=4M q=3 case, ensure d2=11549.
